Print method for Finite Filters Objects

Source: R/print.R
print.finite_filters.Rd

Printing objects of class "finite_filters".

Usage

# S4 method for class 'finite_filters'
print(
  x,
  sfilter = TRUE,
  rfilters = TRUE,
  lfilters = FALSE,
  zero_as_na = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'finite_filters'
show(object)

# S3 method for class 'finite_filters'
as.matrix(
  x,
  sfilter = TRUE,
  rfilters = TRUE,
  lfilters = FALSE,
  zero_as_na = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x, object

An object of class "finite_filters".

sfilter, rfilters, lfilters

Logical indicating whether to add the symmetric filter (sfilter = TRUE by default), the right filters (rfilters = TRUE by default) or the left filters (lfilters = FALSE by default).

zero_as_na

Logical. Asymmetric filters have fewer terms than the symmetric filter. If TRUE, the missing past/future terms in the matrix representation are filled with NA instead of 0. Defaults to FALSE.

...

Further arguments to be passed to or from methods.

Value

The print method returns the argument x, invisibly, as for all base::print() methods.

as.matrix.finite_filters() returns a matrix containing the coefficients of the symmetric and asymmetric filters. The columns are named according to the number of future points used (for right filters). For example, column q=0 corresponds to the asymmetric filter using no future points, while q=1 corresponds to the filter using one future point, and so on. A similar convention with negative values is used for left filters (when printed).

Details

The print method just calls the as.matrix() method and prints the resulting matrix.

See also

finite_filters().

Examples

ff_lp <- lp_filter()
as.matrix(ff_lp)
